title: Power Pages: self-service site ownership transfer in the admin centre
summary: Hold: the audit API note incorrectly leaves the content type unresolved, although Microsoft's API reference assigns workloads outside Entra, Exchange and SharePoint to Audit.General. The transfer steps, recipient requirements, managed-identity exception and corrected Microsoft Graph request are supported.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Power Pages supports self-service ownership transfer without a support request.
claims.quote: Existing site owners and global administrators can assign ownership to another valid user within the tenant without requiring manual intervention from support.

claims.where: front matter: status; summary; What's changing
claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched"

claims.claim: The roadmap target date is September CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "September CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is September CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "September CY2026"

claims.claim: The record lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote:
"releasePhase": [
    "General Availability",
    "Preview"
  ]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
The roadmap lists no US Government cloud.

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Scope: Rollout
claims.claim: The capability is on automatically for admins, makers and marketers, rather than requiring enablement.
claims.quote: Enabled for admins/makers/marketers automatically

claims.claim: The roadmap describes the feature as applying to eligible sites without defining that eligibility.
claims.quote: Power Pages now supports secure site ownership transfer for eligible sites.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap names existing site owners and global administrators as able to transfer ownership within the tenant.
claims.quote: Existing site owners and global administrators can assign ownership to another valid user within the tenant without requiring manual intervention from support.

claims.claim: The roadmap requires the new owner to have appropriate environment access.
claims.quote: The new owner must be a valid user with appropriate access to the environment.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes an auditable ownership-transfer history.
claims.quote: Every ownership transfer is recorded in an auditable history, including the previous owner, new owner, initiating user, and timestamp.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The roadmap says notifications go to the previous owner, new owner and administrators.
claims.quote: Notifications are sent to the previous owner, the new owner, and administrators to ensure transparency and continuity and the changes get logged into Compliance Center.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap describes Power Advisor surfacing sites without a valid owner.
claims.quote: Power Pages also identifies sites that no longer have a valid owner and surfaces this information on Power Advisor.

claims.claim: The roadmap links accountable ownership and transfers to reassignments, role changes and employee departures.
claims.quote: Your organization needs a reliable way to transfer ownership of Power Pages sites when responsibilities change due to team reassignments, role changes, or employee departures.

claims.claim: Transfer is under Power Platform admin center > Manage > Power Pages > site > Site Details > Edit > Owner.
claims.quote:
select **Manage**, and then select **Power Pages**.
3. Select the Power Pages site that you want to update.
4. On the **Site Details** page, select **Edit**.

claims.claim: Remove the current Owner, select the new owner, Save and confirm with Transfer.
claims.quote:
In the **Owner** field, remove the current owner and search for the new owner.
6. Select the new owner, and then select **Save**.
7. Review the confirmation message, and then select **Transfer**.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The selected new owner becomes the site's primary owner.
claims.quote: The new owner becomes the primary owner of the site.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The previous owner might lose access depending on site permissions and configuration.
claims.quote: Depending on the site's permissions and configuration, the previous owner might lose access to the site.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: risk
claims.claim: There is no automatic undo; an authorised administrator must transfer ownership back.
claims.quote: You can't automatically undo an ownership transfer. To restore the previous owner, an authorized administrator must transfer ownership back to that user.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The documented prerequisites require website app ownership plus System administrator, Dynamics 365 administrator or Power Platform administrator.
claims.quote:
You are the website app owner and have any one of the following roles:
    - System administrator
    - Dynamics 365 administrator
    - Power Platform administrator

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Managed-identity sites do not require web app ownership; other sites can hide the option if the administrator is not the web app owner.
claims.quote: model don't need web app ownership as a prerequisite for initiating transfer. For other portals, if you don't see the ownership transfer option, check whether you're the web app owner.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Administrative roles must be directly assigned rather than inherited through security groups or PIM.
claims.quote: a user must be directly assigned to the required role. These roles aren't inherited from security group membership or through privileged identity management (PIM).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope; Governance guidance; front matter: licensing.notes
claims.claim: The recipient must be an enabled Microsoft Entra user of Member user type, not Guest user type.
claims.quote: The new owner is an enabled Microsoft Entra user with a **Member** user type.

claims.claim: The administrator must have access to the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: You have access to the [Power Platform admin center](https://aka.ms/ppac).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The transfer prerequisites do not name Global administrator, unlike the roadmap.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages transfer site ownership disable tenant setting approval workflow. Opened /power-pages/admin/transfer-ownership and /admin-roles; the transfer role lists name System, Dynamics 365 and Power Platform administrators, not Global administrator.

claims.claim: The Learn ownership-transfer page carries no preview label.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/admin/transfer-ownership transfer ownership Power Pages. Opened the complete transfer-ownership page; it has no preview label.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft Purview exposes Transfer site ownership as the searchable OwnershipTransferred operation.
claims.quote: | Transfer site ownership | `OwnershipTransferred` | Ownership of the site is transferred to another user. |

claims.claim: The audit UI is Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Audit.
claims.quote: On the left navigation pane, select **Solutions** and then select **Audit**.

claims.claim: GET {root}/subscriptions/content?contentType={ContentType}&startTime={0}&endTime={1} lists available audit content.
claims.quote:
| **Path** | `/subscriptions/content?contentType={ContentType}&startTime={0}&endTime={1}` |
GET {root}/subscriptions/content?contentType=Audit.SharePoint&PublisherIdentifier=46b472a7-c68e-4adf-8ade-3db49497518e

claims.claim: Listing content requires an active subscription.
claims.quote: An error is returned if the subscription status is disabled.

claims.claim: The listing returns content URIs that must be retrieved to examine the events.
claims.quote: **contentUri**: The URL to use when retrieving the content.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls table: Audit trail of site ownership transfers
claims.claim: Learn does not state which content type holds Power Pages events.
claims.quote:
- Audit.AzureActiveDirectory
- Audit.Exchange
- Audit.SharePoint
- Audit.General (includes all other workloads not included in the previous content types)
claims.fix: Replace 'Learn does not state which content type holds Power Pages events' in controls[1].note and the rendered table with 'Audit.General covers workloads other than Microsoft Entra, Exchange and SharePoint'. The cited API reference states this catch-all scope; Power Pages is outside those three workloads. Keep the existing content-listing call and its placeholders.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; controls[2].note
claims.claim: Viewing Power Pages activity requires configuring auditing for the production environments to monitor.
claims.quote: [Configure and turn on auditing for the Power Platform production environments you want to monitor]

claims.claim: The audit-logging option is visible only when minimum Office licensing requirements are met.
claims.quote: The option to turn on audit logging is only visible when the minimum Office licensing requirements are met.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Reading the logs requires Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs in Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: either the *Audit Logs* or *View-Only Audit Logs* role in Microsoft Purview

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: SAS logging is under Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Privacy and Security > Storage Shared Access Signature (SAS) Security Settings > Enable SAS Logging in Purview.
claims.quote:
Expand the **Product** list and select **Privacy and Security**.
7. In the **Storage Shared Access Signature (SAS) Security Settings** section, toggle the **Enable SAS Logging in Purview** setting to **On**.

claims.claim: PATCH https://api.powerplatform.com/environmentmanagement/environments/{environmentId}/settings/?api-version=2022-03-01-preview with LoggingEnabledForIpBasedStorageAccessSignature true updates SAS logging.
claims.quote:
"LoggingEnabledForIpBasedStorageAccessSignature" = $true
Invoke-WebRequest -Method Patch -Uri "https://api.powerplatform.com/environmentmanagement/environments/$environmentId/settings/?api-version=2022-03-01-preview" -Headers $Headers -Body $body

claims.claim: The environment-management API tutorial uses a preview API.
claims.quote: This tutorial demonstrates how to use the Power Platform API (preview) to create, update, and list Environment Management Settings.

claims.claim: The SAS prerequisite is to allow-list https://*.api.powerplatformusercontent.com or most SAS functionality will not work.
claims.quote: Before you activate the Shared Access Signature (SAS) feature, add the `https://*.api.powerplatformusercontent.com` domain to the allow list. If you don't, most SAS functionalities won't work.

claims.claim: The SAS logging UI instructions say to sign in as a system admin.
claims.quote: Sign in to the [Power Platform admin center](https://admin.preview.powerplatform.microsoft.com/home) as a system admin.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing specific to ownership transfer is not yet published, so the feature's licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages ownership transfer license pricing charge meter. Opened transfer-ownership and powerapps-flow-licensing-faq; read Power Pages licensing and pay-as-you-go meter search excerpts. No transfer-specific licence requirement was found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The transfer page's prerequisite list names roles, portal access and the recipient user type, but no licence.
claims.quote:
You have access to the [Power Platform admin center](https://aka.ms/ppac).
- The new owner is an enabled Microsoft Entra user with a **Member** user type.

claims.claim: No meter or charge specifically for the ownership-transfer operation is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages ownership transfer license pricing charge meter. Opened transfer-ownership and licensing FAQs; read pay-as-you-go-meters excerpts describing website active users, not transfers. No transfer meter or charge was found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Power Pages website licensing is capacity-based, measured as authenticated and anonymous users per website per month.
claims.quote: Power Pages (formerly Power Apps portals) licensing is capacity based and offers two types of capacities based on user type: **Authenticated users per website/month** and **Anonymous users per website/month**.

claims.claim: The licensing FAQs say nothing about ownership transfers.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages ownership transfer license pricing charge meter; searched the fetched powerapps-flow-licensing-faq text for ownership and transfer and read its Power Pages licensing passages. No ownership-transfer licensing passage appeared.

claims.where: Governance controls: website app owner explanation; controls[3].note
claims.claim: Website app ownership is ownership of the website's Entra application registration, separate from the listed administrative roles.
claims.quote: A *website app owner* is a user who owns the website [application registration] in the [Azure portal]

claims.claim: Add website app owners through Azure portal > Microsoft Entra ID > Manage > App registrations > website app > Manage > Owners > Add owners.
claims.quote:
Search for and select **Microsoft Entra ID**.
3. Under **Manage**, select **App registrations**.
4. Select the website app from the list of available applications.
5. Under **Manage**, select **Owners**.
6. Select **Add owners**.

claims.claim: The website application is named Portals-<website name>.
claims.quote: This application is called `Portals-<<website name>>`.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/applications/{id}/owners/$ref with an @odata.id directoryObjects reference adds the indicated application owner.
The Graph reference is a general application-owner operation that accepts individual users, not a Power Pages transfer operation.
claims.quote: Add an owner to an [application]. Application owners can be individual users, the associated service principal, or another service principal.

claims.quote: under **Manage** > **Inventory**. Filtering the **Item type** column to sites limits the grid to Power Pages sites.

claims.claim: Azure Resource Graph KQL PowerPlatformResources | where type =~ "microsoft.powerpages/sites" selects site inventory records.
claims.quote:
The following examples use Kusto Query Language (KQL) against the `PowerPlatformResources` table in Azure Resource Graph.
PowerPlatformResources
| where type =~ "microsoft.powerpages/sites"

claims.claim: Inventory exposes site owner object IDs rather than user display names.
claims.quote:
Owner (`properties.ownerId`)
User identifiers are object IDs, not user display names.

claims.claim: Inventory requires Global administrator, Power Platform administrator or Dynamics 365 administrator.
claims.quote:
One of the following Microsoft Entra roles:
    - Global administrator
    - Power Platform administrator
    - Dynamics 365 administrator

claims.claim: Power Pages inventory is preview and is rolling out gradually, so some regions might not have it.
claims.quote:
This feature is in preview.
- This feature is being rolled out gradually across regions and might not be available yet in your region.

claims.claim: The inventory grid can be filtered by owner to review a particular user's sites.
claims.quote: filter by environment to review sites in a specific environment, by owner to review a user's sites, or by creation date to review recently created sites.

claims.claim: The displayed inventory query does not itself produce a list of sites whose owners are no longer valid.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages ownership transfer notifications Power Advisor ownerless sites recommendation; "Power Advisor" "owner" "Power Pages". Opened power-pages-inventory: its query filters site resource type and returns owner IDs, not owner validity.

claims.claim: No documented PowerShell, Graph or other API equivalent to the admin-centre site-ownership-transfer workflow was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages site ownership transfer API PowerShell pac pages Power Platform API Dataverse ownerid bulk transfer. Opened transfer-ownership, Websites API, pac power-pages and powerpagesite reference; record Assign is documented, but not equivalence to this workflow.

claims.claim: No automated or bulk version of the documented ownership-transfer workflow was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages site ownership transfer API PowerShell pac pages Power Platform API Dataverse ownerid bulk transfer. Opened transfer-ownership, Websites API and pac power-pages; no automated or bulk ownership-transfer workflow was documented.

claims.where: controls[5]; Scope: Rollout; Governance controls; summary
claims.claim: No tenant-wide switch to disable site ownership transfer is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages transfer site ownership disable tenant setting approval workflow. Read transfer-ownership and the control-site-creation search excerpt; the latter disables creation, not ownership transfer. No transfer-disable UI or API was found.

claims.claim: No separate approval workflow for ownership transfer is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages transfer site ownership disable tenant setting approval workflow. Opened transfer-ownership and admin-roles; the transfer procedure ends with the initiating administrator's confirmation, with no separate approver or approval API.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not document the roadmap's transfer notifications or notification controls.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages ownership transfer notifications Power Advisor ownerless sites recommendation. Opened transfer-ownership, admin-roles and Power Pages activity logs; no transfer-notification recipients, delivery behaviour or disable control was found.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not document the Power Advisor recommendation for ownerless Power Pages sites described by the roadmap.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Advisor" "owner" "Power Pages"; Power Pages ownership transfer notifications Power Advisor ownerless sites recommendation. Opened transfer-ownership, action-center and power-pages-inventory; no such Power Advisor recommendation was found.

claims.claim: Learn advises verifying that the new owner can access and manage the site.

claims.claim: The roles page says creator ownership cannot change, in apparent conflict with the separate transfer page.
claims.quote: The *website owner* is the user who created the Power Pages website. While you can update website management roles, ownership remains with the creator and can't be transferred or changed.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The documented transfer is a deliberate administrator action affecting the selected site's owners, not an automatic reassignment on rollout.
claims.quote:
Select the new owner, and then select **Save**.
7. Review the confirmation message, and then select **Transfer**.

When the transfer finishes, the selected user becomes the primary owner of the site.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist names baseline auditing and domain allow-list configuration without corresponding controls-table rows.
claims.quote: Add `https://*.api.powerplatformusercontent.com` to your domain allow list, then turn on auditing and **Enable SAS Logging in Purview**
claims.fix: Remove the domain allow-list and baseline-auditing setup instructions from the checklist, leaving 'Turn on Enable SAS Logging in Purview for the production environments that host Power Pages sites.' Keep the verified prerequisite warning in controls[2].note; its row documents only SAS logging, not the other two configuration steps.
